newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - Nov 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - Nov 27.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- MING PAO DAILY -- The government's decision to introduce subversion laws before the handover to help calm post-handover concerns attracted severe attacks from Beijing.
-- The Chinese postal industry is estimated to lose seven billion yuan this year.
-- TA KUNG PAO -- Chinese President Jiang Zemin met Philippine President Fidel Ramos and reached an agreement on co-developing disputed islands in the South China Sea.
-- Eleven Canadian companies signed contracts related to building the Qinshan nuclear power facility with their Chinese partners in Shanghai, worth a total of US$96 million.

-- EXPRESS NEWS -- The director of China's Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office, Lu Ping, said he had not heard of any members of the Selection Committee who had complained to Beijing about the nomination of the provisional legislation.

-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC TIMES -- Guangzhou International Trust and Investment Corp denied that acquiring shares in Hualing Holdings was a decision of the Guangzhou municipal government. It said it viewed the move as a long-term investment.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Taiwanese state oil monopoly Chinese Petroleum Corp had stalled plans for joint oil exploration with the mainland following calls on the island to reduce economic ties with China.
-- China's experiment with build-operate-transfer projects had reached its second stage, with Junshan bridge due to submit a feasibility study this week.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Amoy Properties raised HK$3.44 billion gross through a share placement and a new share issue to finance new projects and pay off bank loans and share dividends.
